Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=shrine ranking system}}, it was formerly classified as a village shrine. It is designated a {{ill|Kinpei-sha|Q119929592|qid=Q119929592|lt=Shirohei-sha}} by the Gifu Prefecture Association of Shinto Shrines. {{nihongo|'''Shirahige Shrine'''|白鬚神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

It is one of the candidate shrines (ronsa) for Kawashima Shrine of Kawashima in {{ill|Haguri District|hu|Haguri körzet|ja|葉栗郡|ko|하구리군 (아이치현)|pl|Powiat Haguri|sr|Област Хагури|zh|葉栗郡|qid=Q1032507}}, * {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|Q3090037|qid=Q3090037|lt=Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto}} (さるたひこのみこと)<ref name="案内"/>
* {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602}} (あまてらすおおみかみ)<ref name="案内"/>

== History ==
[[File:Shirahige-jinja Kawashima ac (2).jpg|thumb|Main hall built atop high stone walls]]

The date of foundation is unknown. According to shrine tradition, it was established in the 10th year of the {{ill|Yang Water Rat|Q904972|qid=Q904972}} era of Emperor {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|Q313119|qid=Q313119}} following an imperial decree<ref>If taken as the 10th year of Emperor Nintoku’s reign, this would correspond to 322.</ref>, and a shrine building was constructed in the 4th year of the {{ill|Yin Wood Rabbit|Q904791|qid=Q904791}} era of Emperor {{ill|Emperor Ingyō|Q349258|qid=Q349258}} following another imperial decree<ref>If taken as the 4th year of Emperor Ingyō’s reign, this would correspond to 415.</ref><ref name="由緒">Explanatory signboard “History of Shirahige Shrine.”</ref>{{sfn|Kawashima Town|1982|p=1174}}.

In the 2nd year of {{ill|Reiki (era)|Q1373115|qid=Q1373115}} (717), Hachiman Shrine was established as a subordinate shrine within the precincts<ref name="八幡神社">From the inscription on the monument marking the former site of Hachiman Shrine within the grounds of the Inaba District Gymnasium, Kakamigahara City.</ref>{{sfn|Kawashima Town|1982|p=1174}}.

In {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 14 (1586), flooding of the {{ill|Kiso River|Q779607|qid=Q779607}} washed away the shrine buildings. As a result of this flood, a new course of the Kiso River became the boundary between {{ill|Owari Province|ar|أواري|ca|Província d'Owari|ckb|پارێزگای ئۆوواری|cs|Provincie Owari|de|Provinz Owari|es|Provincia de Owari|eu|Owari probintzia|fa|ولایت اوواری|fi|Owarin provinssi|fr|Province d'Owari|gl|Provincia de Owari|hak|Owari-koet|id|Provinsi Owari|it|Owari (provincia)|ja|尾張国|ko|오와리국|lt|Ovario žemė|nl|Owari (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Owari|pt|Província de Owari|ru|Овари (провинция)|simple|Owari Province|sk|Owari (provincia)|sr|Провинција Овари|tr|Owari (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Оварі|vi|Tỉnh Owari|wuu|尾张国|zh|尾張國|zh_min_nan|Owari-kok|zh_yue|尾張國|qid=Q514506}} and {{ill|Mino Province|Q864156|qid=Q864156}}, and this area changed from Haguri District, Owari Province, to {{ill|Haguri district|Q11610214|qid=Q11610214}}, Mino Province. The subordinate Hachiman Shrine was relocated to Majima in Haguri District (present-day {{ill|Kakamigahara|ar|كاكاميغهارا (غيفو)|arz|كاكاميجاهارا, جيفو|azb|کاکامیقاهارا، قیفو|ca|Kakamigahara|ce|Какамигахара|ceb|Kakamigahara (lungsod sa Hapon)|cs|Kakamigahara|de|Kakamigahara|eo|Kakamigahara|es|Kakamigahara (Gifu)|fa|کاکامیگاهارا، گیفو|fi|Kakamigahara|fr|Kakamigahara|gl|Kakamigahara|it|Kakamigahara|ja|各務原市|ko|가카미가하라시|mg|Kakamigahara|mr|काकामिगहारा|mzn|کاکامیگاهارا، گیفو|nl|Kakamigahara|no|Kakamigahara|pl|Kakamigahara|pt|Kakamigahara|ro|Kakamigahara|ru|Какамигахара|sh|Kakamigahara|sr|Какамигахара|su|Kakamigahara, Gifu|sv|Kakamigahara|tg|Какамигаҳара|tl|Kakamigahara, Gifu|tr|Kakamigahara|tt|Какамигахара|uk|Какаміґахара|ur|کاکامیگاہارا، گیفو|vi|Kakamigahara, Gifu|war|Kakamigahara, Gifu|zh|各务原市|zh_classical|各務原市|zh_min_nan|Kakamigahara-chhī|zh_yue|各務原|qid=Q641491}} Kamiochi-chō, at the site of the {{ill|Kakamigahara City Inaba District Gymnasium|Q109603254|qid=Q109603254}})<ref name="八幡神社"/>. Thereafter, it was moved to its present location in Kasada, Haguri District, by {{ill|Tsubouchi Toshisada|Q11425729|qid=Q11425729}}, a {{ill|Shinkanō Jin'ya|Q11501438|qid=Q11501438}} of high rank stationed at {{ill|Shinkanō Jin'ya|Q11501438|qid=Q11501438}} (former lord of {{ill|Matsukura Castle|Q11239240|qid=Q11239240|lt=Matsukura Castle}})<ref name="由緒"/>{{sfn|Kawashima Town|1982|p=1174}}. It was renamed Shirahige Myōjin and later changed to Shirahige Shrine.

During the Meiji period, it became a village shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}. After World War II, it was designated a {{ill|Kinpei-sha|Q119929592|qid=Q119929592|lt=Shirohei-sha}} by the Gifu Prefecture Association of Shinto Shrines.

In 1999 (Heisei 11), the worship hall, norito hall, main hall, {{ill|banpei|Q124160302|qid=Q124160302}}, and other structures were newly built, and Shinmei Shrine was enshrined together<ref>The former location was 1266 Koyabajima, Kasada-chō. It is now within {{ill|Water Eco Park|Q11553849|qid=Q11553849}}.</ref>.

== Subordinate shrines ==
Originally, there were two subordinate shrines: Kaijin Shrine and Akiba Shrine{{sfn|Kawashima Town|1982|p=1174}}. In 1996 (Heisei 8), nearby shrines were absorbed and incorporated as subordinate shrines.

* Kaijin Shrine (Deity: {{ill|Watatsumi|abstract|Q1474187|az|Vatatsumi|de|Watatsumi|es|Watatsumi|fa|واتاتسومی|fr|Watatsumi|hu|Vatacumi|ja|ワタツミ|ko|와타쓰미|mni|ꯋꯇꯠꯁꯨꯃꯤ|pl|Watatsumi|ru|Ватацуми|simple|Watatsumi|uk|Вататсумі|zh|綿津見|qid=Q1474187|lt=Sokotsu Watatsumi-no-Kami}})<ref name="案内">From the on-site information board of “Shirahige Shrine.”</ref>
* Akiba Shrine (Deity: {{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|Q1640658|qid=Q1640658|lt=Hi-no-Kagutsuchi-no-Kami}})<ref name="案内"/>
* Suijin Shrine (Deity: {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602}})<ref name="案内"/><ref>A shrine enshrined at the site of a levee breach caused by flooding. It was later relocated for river improvement and levee construction. In this area, Suijin Shrines sometimes enshrine deities other than {{ill|Suijin|Q3137449|qid=Q3137449}} (such as Amaterasu), possibly because they also serve the purpose of warding off flood damage.</ref>
* Inari Shrine (Deity: {{ill|Ukanomitama|lt=Ukanomitama|Q3080728|qid=Q3080728|qid=Q3080728|lt=Ukanomitama-no-Kami}})<ref name="案内"/>
* Konpira Shrine (Deity: {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto}})<ref name="案内"/>
